tasks.title: Design and implement agentic loops for autonomous task execution
knowledge: Loop lifecycle: send request, inspect `stop_reason` (`"tool_use"` vs `"end_turn"`), run tools, return results for the next iteration
Tool results are appended to the conversation history so the model can reason about the next action
Model-driven tool choice vs pre-configured decision trees
Anti-patterns: parsing natural language to end the loop, iteration caps as the main stopping rule, checking assistant text for completion words
skills: Continue while `stop_reason` is `"tool_use"`, stop on `"end_turn"`
Add tool results to the context between iterations
Avoid natural-language parsing for termination

tasks.title: Orchestrate multi-agent systems with coordinator-subagent patterns
knowledge: Hub-and-spoke: the coordinator manages all inter-subagent communication, error handling and routing
Subagents have isolated context and don't inherit the coordinator's history
Coordinator role: decompose, delegate, aggregate, and pick which subagents to invoke based on query complexity
Overly narrow task decomposition leaves broad topics incompletely covered
skills: Coordinators that select subagents dynamically rather than always running the full pipeline
Partition research scope across subagents to minimise duplication
Iterative refinement: evaluate the synthesis, re-delegate for gaps, repeat until sufficient
Route all communication through the coordinator for observability and consistent error handling

tasks.title: Configure subagent invocation, context passing, and spawning
knowledge: The `Task` tool spawns subagents; a coordinator's `allowedTools` must include `"Task"`
Subagent context must be given explicitly in the prompt; no automatic inheritance or shared memory
`AgentDefinition`: description, system prompt and tool restrictions per subagent type
`fork_session` explores divergent approaches from a shared baseline
skills: Pass complete findings from earlier agents in the subagent prompt
Use structured formats that separate content from metadata (URLs, page numbers) for attribution
Spawn parallel subagents with several `Task` calls in one coordinator response
Give coordinators goals and quality criteria, not step-by-step procedures

tasks.title: Implement multi-step workflows with enforcement and handoff patterns
knowledge: Programmatic enforcement (hooks, prerequisite gates) vs prompt guidance for workflow ordering
When compliance must be deterministic (identity check before money moves), prompts alone have a non-zero failure rate
Structured handoff protocol: customer ID, root-cause analysis, recommended actions
skills: Prerequisites that block downstream tools until earlier steps complete (block `process_refund` until `get_customer` returns a verified ID)
Split multi-concern requests into items, investigate in parallel, synthesise one resolution
Compile structured handoff summaries when escalating to humans

tasks.title: Apply Agent SDK hooks for tool call interception and data normalization
knowledge: `PostToolUse` hooks transform tool results before the model sees them
Hooks on outgoing tool calls enforce compliance (e.g. block refunds above a threshold)
Hooks are deterministic; prompt instructions are probabilistic
skills: Normalise mixed formats (Unix timestamps, ISO 8601, numeric status codes) from different MCP tools in a `PostToolUse` hook
Block policy-violating actions and redirect to another workflow such as human escalation
Choose hooks over prompts when business rules need guaranteed compliance

tasks.title: Design task decomposition strategies for complex workflows
knowledge: Fixed sequential pipelines (prompt chaining) vs dynamic decomposition driven by intermediate findings
Prompt chaining for reviews: analyse each file, then a cross-file integration pass
Adaptive investigation plans generate subtasks from what each step discovers
skills: Prompt chaining for predictable multi-aspect reviews; dynamic decomposition for open-ended investigation
Split large reviews into per-file passes plus a cross-file pass
For open-ended tasks: map the structure, find high-impact areas, then make a prioritised plan that adapts

tasks.title: Manage session state, resumption, and forking
knowledge: `--resume <session-name>` continues a specific earlier conversation
`fork_session` creates independent branches from a shared analysis baseline
Tell a resumed agent which previously analysed files have changed
A fresh start with a structured summary is more reliable than resuming with stale tool results
skills: Use `--resume` with named sessions to continue investigations
Use `fork_session` to compare approaches in parallel branches
Resume when prior context is mostly valid; start fresh with an injected summary when tool results are stale
Tell resumed sessions about specific file changes for targeted re-analysis

tasks.title: Design effective tool interfaces with clear descriptions and boundaries
knowledge: Tool descriptions are the main signal for tool selection; minimal descriptions make selection unreliable
Good descriptions include input formats, example queries, edge cases and boundaries
Overlapping descriptions (`analyze_content` vs `analyze_document`) cause misrouting
System-prompt wording can create keyword-sensitive tool associations
skills: Write descriptions that separate each tool's purpose, inputs, outputs and when to use it instead of the alternatives
Rename tools and rewrite descriptions to remove overlap
Split generic tools into purpose-specific tools with defined contracts
Review system prompts for keyword instructions that override good tool descriptions

tasks.title: Implement structured error responses for MCP tools
knowledge: MCP `isError` flag signals tool failure to the agent
Error kinds: transient (timeout), validation (bad input), business (policy), permission
Uniform errors ("Operation failed") prevent good recovery decisions
Retryable vs non-retryable metadata prevents wasted retries
skills: Return `errorCategory`, `isRetryable` and a readable description
For business-rule violations return `retriable: false` with a customer-friendly explanation
Recover locally from transient failures; pass only unresolvable errors to the coordinator
Tell access failures apart from valid empty results

tasks.title: Distribute tools appropriately across agents and configure tool choice
knowledge: Too many tools (18 instead of 4–5) makes selection less reliable
Agents with tools outside their role tend to misuse them
Scoped access: give each agent only the tools its role needs
`tool_choice`: `"auto"` (may return text), `"any"` (must call a tool), forced `{"type":"tool","name":...}`
skills: Restrict each subagent's tools to its role
Replace generic tools with constrained ones (`fetch_url` → `load_document` that validates URLs)
Give scoped cross-role tools (`verify_fact` for synthesis) and route complex cases through the coordinator
Force a specific tool to run first; use `"any"` to guarantee a tool call rather than text

tasks.title: Integrate MCP servers into Claude Code and agent workflows
knowledge: Project `.mcp.json` for shared team servers vs user `~/.claude.json` for personal or experimental ones
Environment variable expansion in `.mcp.json` (`${GITHUB_TOKEN}`) keeps secrets out of git
Tools from all configured servers are discovered at connection time and available together
MCP resources expose content catalogs (issues, docs, schemas) and cut exploratory tool calls
skills: Configure shared servers in project `.mcp.json` with env expansion
Configure personal servers in `~/.claude.json`
Improve MCP tool descriptions so agents don't prefer built-ins like Grep over a more capable MCP tool
Prefer existing community servers over custom builds for standard integrations

tasks.title: Select and apply built-in tools (Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Grep, Glob) effectively
knowledge: Grep searches file contents (function names, error messages, imports)
Glob matches file paths (names, extensions)
Read/Write for whole files; Edit for targeted changes anchored on unique text
When Edit fails on a non-unique match, fall back to Read + Write
skills: Pick Grep for content and Glob for path patterns
Use Read + Write when Edit can't find a unique anchor
Build understanding incrementally: Grep for entry points, Read to follow imports
Trace usage through wrapper modules by finding exported names, then searching for them

tasks.title: Configure CLAUDE.md files with appropriate hierarchy, scoping, and modular organization
knowledge: Hierarchy: user `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`, project `.claude/CLAUDE.md` or root `CLAUDE.md`, subdirectory `CLAUDE.md`
User-level files apply only to that user and aren't shared through git
`@import` references other files to keep CLAUDE.md modular
`.claude/rules/` holds topic-specific rule files instead of one large CLAUDE.md
skills: Diagnose hierarchy issues (team instructions placed at user level)
Use `@import` to include standards files per package
Split a large CLAUDE.md into `.claude/rules/` topic files
Use `/memory` to see which files are loaded

tasks.title: Create and configure custom slash commands and skills
knowledge: Project commands in `.claude/commands/` (shared via git) vs user commands in `~/.claude/commands/`
Skills in `.claude/skills/` with `SKILL.md` frontmatter: `context: fork`, `allowed-tools`, `argument-hint`
`context: fork` runs the skill in an isolated sub-agent so its output doesn't flood the main conversation
Personal skill variants go in `~/.claude/skills/` under different names
skills: Create project commands for team-wide availability
Use `context: fork` for verbose or exploratory skills
Restrict tools with `allowed-tools`; prompt for parameters with `argument-hint`
Choose skills (on demand) vs CLAUDE.md (always loaded)

tasks.title: Apply path-specific rules for conditional convention loading
knowledge: `.claude/rules/` files with YAML frontmatter `paths` glob patterns
Path-scoped rules load only when matching files are edited, saving context
Glob rules beat subdirectory CLAUDE.md files for conventions spread across directories
skills: Scope rules with frontmatter such as `paths: ["terraform/**/*"]`
Apply conventions by file type anywhere (`**/*.test.tsx`)
Choose path rules over subdirectory CLAUDE.md for cross-cutting conventions

tasks.title: Determine when to use plan mode vs direct execution
knowledge: Plan mode for large changes, several valid approaches, architectural decisions, multi-file edits
Direct execution for simple, well-scoped changes (single-file bug fix, one validation check)
Plan mode allows safe exploration before committing to changes
The Explore subagent isolates verbose discovery and returns a summary
skills: Plan mode for microservice restructuring or 45+ file migrations
Direct execution for well-understood changes
Explore subagent to avoid exhausting context during discovery
Plan mode to investigate, then direct execution to implement

tasks.title: Apply iterative refinement techniques for progressive improvement
knowledge: Concrete input/output examples communicate transformations best when prose is read inconsistently
Test-driven iteration: write tests first, then iterate by sharing failures
Interview pattern: Claude asks questions to surface considerations the developer missed
Send interacting problems together in one message; iterate sequentially on independent ones
skills: Give 2–3 concrete I/O examples
Write tests for behaviour, edge cases and performance before implementing
Use the interview pattern in unfamiliar domains
Fix edge cases by giving specific inputs and expected outputs

tasks.title: Integrate Claude Code into CI/CD pipelines
knowledge: `-p` / `--print` runs Claude Code non-interactively
`--output-format json` and `--json-schema` give structured output in CI
CLAUDE.md supplies project context (testing standards, review criteria) to CI runs
Session isolation: the session that wrote the code is worse at reviewing it
skills: Use `-p` so CI never hangs waiting for input
Use `--output-format json` with `--json-schema` for machine-parseable findings
Include earlier findings when re-reviewing after new commits to avoid duplicate comments
Provide existing tests in context so suggestions don't duplicate them; document fixtures in CLAUDE.md

tasks.title: Design prompts with explicit criteria to improve precision and reduce false positives
knowledge: Explicit criteria beat vague instructions ("flag comments only when claimed behaviour contradicts the code")
"Be conservative" or "only high-confidence findings" fail compared with specific categorical criteria
A high false-positive rate in one category undermines trust in accurate categories
skills: Define which issues to report (bugs, security) and which to skip (minor style, local patterns)
Temporarily disable high false-positive categories to restore trust
Define severity levels with concrete code examples

tasks.title: Apply few-shot prompting to improve output consistency and quality
knowledge: Few-shot examples are the most effective way to get consistently formatted, actionable output
Examples show how to handle ambiguous cases
Examples help generalisation to new patterns, not just listed cases
Examples reduce hallucination in extraction across varied document structures
skills: Write 2–4 targeted examples for ambiguous cases, showing the reasoning
Show the exact output format (location, issue, severity, fix)
Show acceptable patterns vs genuine issues
Show correct extraction across varied formats to fix empty or null fields

tasks.title: Enforce structured output using tool use and JSON schemas
knowledge: `tool_use` with a JSON schema is the most reliable route to schema-compliant output
`tool_choice`: `"auto"`, `"any"`, or a forced named tool
Strict schemas remove syntax errors but not semantic errors (totals that don't add up, values in wrong fields)
Schema design: required vs optional, enums with `"other"` plus a detail string
skills: Define extraction tools with a JSON schema input and read the `tool_use` block
Use `"any"` when several schemas exist; force `{"type":"tool","name":"extract_metadata"}` for ordering
Make fields nullable so the model doesn't invent missing information
Add `"unclear"` / `"other"` enum values with detail fields; put normalisation rules in the prompt

tasks.title: Implement validation, retry, and feedback loops for extraction quality
knowledge: Retry with error feedback: append the specific validation errors on retry
Retries don't help when the information is absent from the source
A `detected_pattern` field lets you analyse dismissal patterns
Semantic validation errors vs schema syntax errors (the latter removed by tool use)
skills: Retry with the original document, the failed extraction and the specific errors
Recognise when retries will fail (missing data) vs succeed (format mismatch)
Add `detected_pattern` to analyse false positives
Self-check fields: `calculated_total` beside `stated_total`, `conflict_detected` booleans

tasks.title: Design efficient batch processing strategies
knowledge: Message Batches API: 50% cheaper, up to 24-hour window, no latency SLA
Suited to latency-tolerant work (overnight reports, weekly audits, nightly test generation)
Not suited to blocking work such as pre-merge checks
No multi-turn tool calling inside one batch request; `custom_id` correlates requests and responses
skills: Synchronous for blocking, batch for overnight or weekly
Work out submission frequency from the SLA (e.g. 4-hour windows for a 30-hour SLA)
Resubmit only failed items by `custom_id`
Refine the prompt on a sample before batching large volumes

tasks.title: Design multi-instance and multi-pass review architectures
knowledge: Self-review is weak: the model keeps its generation reasoning and rarely questions it
An independent instance without that context catches more subtle issues
Multi-pass review: per-file passes plus cross-file integration passes avoid diluted attention
skills: Review generated code with a second, independent instance
Split large reviews into per-file passes plus an integration pass for cross-file data flow
Run verification passes where the model reports confidence per finding

tasks.title: Manage conversation context to preserve critical information across long interactions
knowledge: Progressive summarisation turns numbers, dates and customer expectations into vague text
"Lost in the middle": the start and end of long inputs are processed reliably, the middle less so
Tool results pile up and consume tokens out of proportion to their relevance (40+ fields when 5 matter)
Send the complete conversation history in each request to stay coherent
skills: Keep a persistent "case facts" block (amounts, dates, order numbers, statuses) outside summarised history
Trim tool outputs to the relevant fields
Put key-findings summaries at the start of aggregated inputs, with clear section headers
Have upstream agents return structured facts and citations instead of verbose content

tasks.title: Design effective escalation and ambiguity resolution patterns
knowledge: Escalation triggers: the customer asks for a human, a policy exception or gap, no meaningful progress
Escalate at once on an explicit demand; offer to resolve when the issue is straightforward
Sentiment and self-reported confidence are unreliable proxies for complexity
Multiple customer matches need a clarifying identifier, not a heuristic pick
skills: Add explicit escalation criteria with few-shot examples to the system prompt
Honour explicit requests for a human immediately
Acknowledge frustration and offer to resolve; escalate if the customer repeats the request
Escalate when policy is silent on the request (competitor price matching); ask for more identifiers on multiple matches

tasks.title: Implement error propagation strategies across multi-agent systems
knowledge: Structured error context (failure type, attempted query, partial results, alternatives) lets the coordinator recover
Access failures vs valid empty results
Generic statuses ("search unavailable") hide context
Silently suppressing errors and ending the whole workflow on one failure are both anti-patterns
skills: Return structured error context with what was attempted and partial results
Distinguish access failures from empty results
Recover locally from transient failures and pass up only what can't be resolved
Annotate synthesis output with coverage: well-supported findings vs gaps from unavailable sources

tasks.title: Manage context effectively in large codebase exploration
knowledge: In long sessions answers degrade and refer to "typical patterns" instead of the classes found earlier
Scratchpad files keep key findings across context boundaries
Subagents isolate verbose exploration while the main agent keeps the overview
Crash recovery: each agent exports state to a known location; the coordinator loads a manifest on resume
skills: Spawn subagents for specific questions ("find all test files", "trace refund flow dependencies")
Keep and consult scratchpad files of findings
Summarise one phase before spawning subagents for the next
Use `/compact` when discovery output fills the context

tasks.title: Design human review workflows and confidence calibration
knowledge: Aggregate accuracy (97% overall) can hide poor results on specific document types or fields
Stratified random sampling measures error rates in high-confidence output and finds new error patterns
Field-level confidence scores calibrated on labelled validation sets route review attention
Validate by document type and field before automating high-confidence extractions
skills: Stratified sampling of high-confidence extractions for ongoing measurement
Analyse accuracy by document type and field before reducing human review
Calibrate review thresholds for field-level confidence on labelled data
Route low-confidence or contradictory documents to human review first

tasks.title: Preserve information provenance and handle uncertainty in multi-source synthesis
knowledge: Attribution is lost when findings are summarised without claim-source mappings
Synthesis must preserve and merge structured claim-source mappings
Conflicting statistics from credible sources are annotated with attribution, not resolved arbitrarily
Publication or collection dates stop time differences being read as contradictions
skills: Have subagents output claim-source mappings (URL, document, excerpt) that survive synthesis
Separate well-established from contested findings in reports
Include conflicting values with annotations and let the coordinator reconcile
Render content by type (financial data as tables, news as prose, technical findings as lists)

scenarios.name: Customer Support Resolution Agent
scenarios.setup: You are building a customer support resolution agent with the Claude Agent SDK. It handles returns, billing disputes and account issues for an online retailer, working through MCP tools such as `get_customer`, `lookup_order`, `process_refund` and `escalate_to_human`. The business target is at least 80% first-contact resolution, while still escalating the cases that need a person. Refunds and account changes move real money, so some rules must hold every time, and conversations can run long across several issues.

scenarios.name: Code Generation with Claude Code
scenarios.setup: Your engineering team uses Claude Code day to day for code generation, refactoring, debugging and documentation in a shared repository. You are responsible for how it is configured: CLAUDE.md files at user, project and directory level, `.claude/rules/`, custom slash commands and skills, and team versus personal settings. Developers also need guidance on when to use plan mode instead of direct execution, and how to iterate with Claude to reach the result they want without wasting context.

scenarios.name: Multi-Agent Research System
scenarios.setup: You are building a multi-agent research system. A coordinator agent breaks each research request into parts and delegates them to specialised subagents: a web search subagent, a document analysis subagent and a report synthesis subagent. The final output is a thorough report with accurate citations. The system must pass the right context to each subagent, cope with partial failures such as timeouts, and keep track of which source supports each claim.

scenarios.name: Developer Productivity with Claude
scenarios.setup: Your platform team gives engineers a Claude-based assistant for exploring unfamiliar codebases, understanding legacy systems and generating boilerplate. It uses Claude Code's built-in tools (Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Grep, Glob) along with MCP servers for internal systems such as the issue tracker and documentation. Codebases are large, sessions can run for hours, and work is often picked up again the next day.

scenarios.name: Claude Code for CI/CD
scenarios.setup: You are integrating Claude Code into the CI/CD pipeline for automated code review, test generation and pull-request feedback. It runs without a human at the keyboard, and its findings are posted as PR comments that developers must trust. Feedback has to be actionable with few false positives. Some jobs block merges and others run overnight, and results must be machine-readable for the pipeline to act on.

scenarios.name: Structured Data Extraction
scenarios.setup: You are building a pipeline that extracts structured data from unstructured documents such as invoices, contracts and research papers. Output is validated against JSON schemas and fed to downstream systems that expect consistent fields. The pipeline must stay accurate across document types, handle missing or ambiguous information without inventing values, process large volumes cost-effectively, and send uncertain cases to human reviewers.
